title: OpenTitan hardening primitives
question: Do OpenTitan's built-in fault countermeasures (multi-bit booleans, redundant counters) still need several bit flips to break after an open-source synthesis tool has built them, and are the redundant parts still there?

example.name: 3 primitives: mubi_flag, mubi_word, count_regs
example.description:
Example (smallest meaningful set, under a minute):
  mubi_flag   prim_mubi4_sender -> sync -> dec: a 4-bit "multi-bit boolean" decoded to one flag
  mubi_word   prim_mubi4_sender -> sync: the 4-bit word itself
  count_regs  prim_count: primary up counter + secondary down counter, a fault makes them disagree

findings.text: OpenTitan multi-bit boolean (prim_mubi4 sender, sync, decoder) ending in one flag: built from the pinned OpenTitan sources with Yosys 0.71 (read_slang) and Yosys 0.33: 65 gates, 17 flip-flops (Yosys 0.71 alone: 64 gates, 17 flip-flops).
findings.label: MEASURED

findings.text: OpenTitan multi-bit boolean (prim_mubi4 sender, sync, decoder) ending in one flag: the smallest attack needs 1 bit flip(s) (model: single-cycle bit flips on gate and flip-flop outputs, up to 3 flips, 6 cycles). Prediction written before the run: 1 (the decoder ends in one gate). Same answer as the recorded run in work/.
findings.label: SIMULATED

findings.text: OpenTitan multi-bit boolean word (prim_mubi4 sender and sync): built from the pinned OpenTitan sources with Yosys 0.71 (read_slang) and Yosys 0.33: 60 gates, 17 flip-flops (Yosys 0.71 alone: 60 gates, 17 flip-flops).
findings.label: MEASURED

findings.text: OpenTitan multi-bit boolean word (prim_mubi4 sender and sync): the smallest attack needs 4 bit flip(s) (model: single-cycle bit flips on gate and flip-flop outputs, up to 6 flips, 6 cycles). Prediction written before the run: none up to 3 (4 output bits, each from its own gate after the stability check). Same answer as the recorded run in work/.
findings.label: SIMULATED

findings.text: OpenTitan prim_count redundant counter pair (up and down copies): built from the pinned OpenTitan sources with Yosys 0.71 (read_slang) and Yosys 0.33: 269 gates, 14 flip-flops (Yosys 0.71 alone: 285 gates, 14 flip-flops).
findings.label: MEASURED

findings.text: OpenTitan prim_count redundant counter pair (up and down copies): the smallest attack needs 2 bit flip(s) (model: single-cycle bit flips on gate and flip-flop outputs, up to 3 flips, 5 cycles). Prediction written before the run: 2 (one bit in each counter, or one counter bit plus err). Same answer as the recorded run in work/.

findings.label: MEASURED

findings.text: The other experiments of experiments.tsv (prim_double_lfsr, AES counter and cipher FSMs, FSM-optimisation flows) are not part of this Labs example.

findings.label: UNTESTED

labels.MEASURED: counted or computed by running real tools on real inputs in this module
labels.SIMULATED: the outcome of a model (fault simulator or probing model); a model, not silicon
labels.UNTESTED: stated or expected, but not checked by any run in this module yet

caveats: Built with open-source Yosys (0.71 read_slang to elaborate, 0.33 to map to generic gates), not with OpenTitan's flow or a real cell library.
Fault model: single-cycle bit flips on gate and flip-flop outputs, bounded number of flips and cycles; a bounded result says nothing beyond those bounds.
Each primitive is analysed alone, in a small wrapper; in a chip, the surrounding logic can help or hurt.
The survival check is structural (are redundant copies still separate nets/registers?), not a proof.
The OpenTitan SystemVerilog is used through small shims for primgen primitives (shims/).

scale.note: BOUNDED: the statement holds for at most 3 single-cycle bit flips (gate outputs and flop Q) within 6 cycles on this netlist. It says nothing about more flips, longer runs, other fault types or physical feasibility. Modelled faults.
